The likes of Uber’s Dara Khosrowshahi and Coatue’s Philippe Laffont have embraced the racket sport. 

And court access can cost nearly $50,000.

Full story: https://t.co/sOcYz80GOq

"investment funds managed by Coatue Management, L.L.C., and Situational Awareness Partners LP (in alphabetical order) (collectively, the “Cornerstone Investors”) have, severally and not jointly, indicated an interest in purchasing up to an aggregate of US$7 billion of the ADSs offered in this offering at the initial public offering price and on the same terms and conditions as the other purchasers in this offering."

SK Hynix will close bookbuilding for its $28 billion offering of ADRs on Wednesday U.S. time, as orders have already covered its ​books multiple times, said a source with knowledge of the matter.

U.S.-based investors came in with chunky orders starting in the range of $200 ​million, the source said, adding larger orders exceeded $1 billion.

Hynix said on Monday that Baillie Gifford Overseas Limited, investment funds managed by Coatue Management and Situational Awareness Partners have each ​separately indicated interest in purchasing up to a combined $7 billion of its U.S. ADRs.

text:
Lucas Swisher (@LucasSwisher1) of Coatue, pushes back on the idea that frontier models are becoming a commodity.

Frontier models continue to improve at a very rapid pace and benefit from access to talent, compute, and training incremental models. https://t.co/cHvkeUIOCj

Coatue is leading @databricks' new strategic funding round.

The company is building what enterprises need to run AI reliably in production: governed data, model choice, cost control, and business context.

The new capital expands that work across Unity AI Gateway, Genie, and Lakebase.

text:
The prior from a portfolio construction perspective feels a lot more like Archegos than it does to Melvin or LTCM.
> 400% gross
> Concentrated, directional, illiquid positions

I don't know all the details obviously, but CNBC reporting SALP was running 400% gross is *unbelievably wild*.

For context, the single manager / Tiger Cub world will generally run in the 150-250% gross range, and even at those levels you saw in '22 some very gnarly net returns (down 40-55%). I don't know that I've ever known a single manager fund to run 400% gross (unless it's a market neutral multi-spin running very tight risk controls).

As far as I can tell, Leopold was running a much more concentrated, much higher octane portfolio than the typical Tiger Cub portfolio, long things like BE/SNDK/CRWV/IREN which we know from the 13F and short things like ADBE which we have learned from reporting). Unfortunately this wasn't bad luck, it was incredibly irresponsible portfolio construction.

And with long book down 30-50% in July, shorts provided little real hedge value: funding shorts like NVDA were flat and alpha shorts like ADBE were +20%. This is the *new normal* in long-short spreads during market kerfuffle as crowding & thematic exposure has become deterministic as strategy crowding has increased over the last 15 years. Hence modern PM mentality that "gross is risk" - see Coatue anticipatory de-grossing in late '21 peak. Effectively, there are only two ways to protect capital in modern kerfuffles: gross down before the storm, or enter the storm with counter-consensus positioning (which is hard, who wants to be long AI losers and short AI winners?)

When VIAC broke and things unraveled at Archegos, primes ended up holding a huge bag (press reporting $10bn+ loses). From my simple, uninformed napkin math, it seems like that could have happened here as well, if not for the Citadel transaction. From 13-F and public reporting (and some of my estimates on short book construction), it looks like the L/S spread unwind peaked at -48% on July 29th. This was a crisis situation and, again, based on public reporting, there was no way of salvaging this: the equity NAV was at risk of going negative (again, what we don't know is how proactively gross was reduced through July). 

SALP should have been a LO/crossover fund from the beginning.

text:
Holy shit this is really bad (and honestly shocking)

Airtable raised at $11.7B in December 2021 from large VCs including Benchmark, Coatue, D1 Capital Partners and Thrive Capital

Now, Bending Spoons is acquiring Airtable for $2.25B but Airtable has $965M of cash, so the real value is $1.285B. Down 90% - bad. 

Airtable had raised $1.35B of VC capital in total, more than what it sold for - very bad. 

And the most surprising and important part, at ~$480M ARR growing 20%+ YoY, that’s 2.7x ARR. Assuming low-30% normalized margins (conservative), that's a 8-9x EBITDA multiple - extremely bad. 

Why did they sell? Realized growth was going to disappear? Retention dropped? Too much S&M to make economics work? 

Curious to see how VCs will update their marks!

NEW EVENT: AI Investing Forum, NYC Sep 17th 

Since our first AI webinar nearly two years ago, I have had the opportunity to have many conversations with builders at the intersection of investing & AI. 

It has been a fascinating project and a fun endeavor for me personally (I love teaching young investors, but the 56th time explaining a P/E ratio doesn't particularly scratch my itch for adventure). 

And my conviction is growing that we are at a key inflection point for AI in the investment process due to three evolving & reinforcing curves:

1) Capability: of frontier models, shifting from answer engines to work engines, and the Fable/Sol/Kimi diffusion moment that is currently happening (particularly around quantitative & Excel read/write capabilities)

2) Economics: of inference, and the ability to create ambient & persistent digital analysts leveraging open-source models with routing to frontier intelligence only where necessary (i.e. I don't need Fable to extract numbers from an 8-K). Throw latency / run-time improvements into this bucket.

3) Connectivity: of institutional-grade context, both external & internal, via the maturation of the MCP pathway, innovation of headless RMS systems, facilitating structures like knowledge graphs & ontologies, and the reducing friction around local model hosting & post-training that appears on the come. Enhanced by much better frontier model adherence to granular Skills.

(It seems obvious to me for as well that the direct LLM approach for investors is structurally flawed and a very exciting application layer for investors is set to emerge, as it has in the legal profession, but that's a tweet for another day).

For a lot of the last ~24 months, my unsatisfying counsel to funds that have sought it is that the best decision on implementing AI could be "wait and watch", stay nimble & ready to lift & shift, for risk of getting run over by Sutton's Bitter Lesson. Nearly every early adopter of AI in Investing has obsoleted early systems (generally with scar tissue of wasted time, money & wasted investor attention/credibility). I believe the time to "wait & watch" is nearing its end, and it is nearing the time to "build aggressively". 

In that spirit, I am founding a new business called Forward Fundamental to take what I'm good at (decomposing investment process, codifying investor taste & investor training and enablement) and help facilitate the emergence of the harness / application layer for investors (more on that later), leaning into our podcast Invest With AI, and working with leading vendors to collaborate on some exciting events & strategic partnerships.

With that said, I am very excited to announce the AI Investing Forum, presented by Fundamental Edge and sponsored by AlphaSense.

The AI Investing Forum is an off the record opportunity to hear from four leading builders at the intersection of AI & Finance:
> Jack Kokko, CEO of AlphaSense
> Dan Bookstaber, Head of Product at Freestone Grove Partners
> Rich Falk-Wallace, CEO of Arcana (fmr Viking/Citadel)
> Alex Izydorczyk, Partner at NX1 (fmr Coatue)

I will kick off the event with a short "State of AI in Investing" presentation then guide the speakers through fireside discussions.

While I expect that portion of the evening to be exceptional, I am really excited to get a group of builders together post firesides for networking, idea sharing & connection. I hosted a small AI mixer over the summer and we had overwhelming demand. It was an exceptional event, and it gave me the bug to think bigger and do more.

So, here we go.

This will be an invitation only event where you can request an invitation. Strong bias is towards attendees actively building AI processes on the asset management side, though we will consider all invitation requests. Thanks to the generosity of AlphaSense, this is a free event.

If this is interesting, please register / request invitation via the link in replies.

Thanks and hope to see you there!

Brett

The deal brings Firmus' total contracted capacity for customers to more than 900 megawatts, agreements that the company says will underpin its expansion in the region.

Founded in 2019, Firmus has undertaken several equity raises over the last year, raising more than $3 billion and valuing the company at more than $10.5 billion. Nvidia has participated in the fundraising along with tech investor Coatue and private equity giant Blackstone, which in February extended $10 billion in debt financing.

Through a partnership with Nvidia, Firmus is deploying that company's chips in facilities based on its Vera Rubin DSX reference design guidelines for building AI infrastructure. The data centers integrate Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale systems with the Firmus-developed HyperCube liquid cooling system that's manufactured in Australia.
